sentences_added: A field served empty is marked on the word that states the emptiness (`search-empty(S): P`, `predicate-empty(S): P`);
an empty field with no such word has nothing to carry a marker and says nothing about its production.
Pin that time with `as_of(t)` when S will be held or relayed.
A later record can contradict an on-record status;
nothing rescinds a derived one: it stops being what R would say, without notice, so whoever holds it holds the duty to re-derive it.
A derived status written back into a stored field is still derived-at-read: storing it makes no record state it.
It is on-record only when the write is itself a record naming R and when R ran, and E is that record.
Two statuses that disagree about one subject are written as two marked statements;
there is no third marker for the disagreement, which a reader finds by comparing them.
